notes: Event monitor: each domain's always block compares the outputs to their previous values on any signal event. It flags a change when the time step has no rising edge of that domain's clock and no falling edge of its reset. The edge test uses current values against the previous ones, so an asynchronous reset that changes an output in the same time step is not a race. The glitch counter is checked with $stable on the domain clock. A second assertion covers the slv domain. Its failures add to fails_CHK_002, but its hits are not counted, so hits_CHK_002 only counts the mst-clock assertion. Changes are checked only after the first clock or reset edge, to ignore X-to-value changes at time 0. Verilator evaluates settled values only, so a true zero-width glitch inside one time step cannot be seen; only a second change in a later time step is detected.
